transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-11
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 52 minutes (recorded)
Attendees: Maya, Carlos, Leah (Redwood) | Jordan, Priya, Samir (Echelon)

Auto Summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
- Finalize pass/fail thresholds for the POC acceptance tests, agree on report rows/metrics, and line up benchmark window.
- Discussed workload sizing: 2-day production trace, peak QPS, 99th/95th latency buckets.
- Action items: Redwood to deliver rubric & report template; customer to share traces and network constraints.

Topics: success criteria, go/no-go thresholds, reporting format, timeline, security considerations

Transcript: (timestamps approximate, transcription imperfect, small overlaps)
[00:00] Maya: okay hey everyone thanks for joining, great to see you, we'll— I'll kick us off, quick agenda: thresholds, report format, timing.
[00:18] Jordan: yep sounds good, sorry I'm on a weird connection — I might drop a smidge.
[00:25] Carlos: no worries, Jordan. Quick clarifying Q: the trace you mentioned in the doc, is that a sample from production or synthetic?
[00:33] Samir: it's production sampled, two full business days, it's redacted PII but otherwise fidelity is real.
[00:40] Leah: perfect, that's ideal for latency percentiles and cache hit profiling.
[00:47] Priya: couple infra notes: we run in us-east and us-west, VPC peering is OK, but any egress needs to go through our firewall stack — so if you need to spin a temporary test endpoint we need IP allowlist.
[00:59] Maya: noted. We'll need the list and any SAML user groups for access.
[01:05] Jordan: SLA success criteria — we really want clear pass/fail so execs can sign off quickly. Suggested: pass if 95th latency < 250ms and P99 < 450ms on tail workloads with 95% of requests matching quality bar.
[01:24] Carlos: hmm those numbers are doable on our dedicated configs but much depends on sequence length and top-k settings. Is the 95% quality bar measured by exact match, clinical accuracy, or human eval?
[01:36] Samir: good question, we want business-level correctness: our 3 prompts should produce answers that match a seeded ground truth set — we can provide 100 labelled examples for the scoring.
[01:47] Leah: okay so the acceptance testing will have two axes: performance (latency/throughput) and quality (labelled F1/accuracy or human pass rate). We'll include a tolerance for model stochasticity — e.g., pass if mean accuracy >= 90% and sample human pass rate >= 88%.
[02:05] Jordan: that seems fair. Do you do reranking or any engineered post-processing in the pipeline? That affects token counts.
[02:12] Samir: yes small post processing, but we can stage both raw model output and post-processed output in the report.
[02:18] Carlos: helpful. For benchmarking we propose: 1) run full trace through model variant A (open weights quantized) and variant B (higher-precision host) 2) collect per-request latency, tokens, cache hits, 95/99 percentiles, model perplexity-ish or logit margin where relevant.
[02:38] Priya: you'll need to ensure traffic from your test runners originates from our approved CIDR. Also we require detailed audit logs for the POC runs for compliance.
[02:46] Maya: we can enable audit-level logging and share a debug bundle — note that for hosted endpoints we redact certain headers, but we can deliver a sanitized log.
[02:55] Jordan: payload sizes vary; some queries hit 2k tokens. We need to include memory pressure cases in acceptance.
[03:03] Carlos: right, we should include a 'long-tail' scenario: the top 5% of sequences over 1k tokens, measure latency and NV mem behaviour. We'll include a separate report section.
[03:13] Samir: what's the go/no-go decision matrix look like? If perf fails but quality passes, do we still accept?
[03:19] Leah: good point. Our recommended matrix (draft):
- Green: quality >= 90% AND 95th <= 250ms AND P99 <= 450ms -> Pass
- Yellow: quality >= 90% but 95th between 250-350ms (or P99 450-600ms) -> Conditional pass with mitigation plan and 2-week follow-up run
- Red: quality < 90% OR P99 > 600ms -> Fail
(we discussed adapt thresholds for dedicated hardware)
[03:47] Jordan: we like that. For Yellow, we will want a documented mitigation and an SLA to re-run benchmarks.
[03:53] Maya: we'll include that in the report template — a 'mitigation & remediation' section with owner and target date.
[03:59] Priya: on reporting format — CSV rows or parquet? Our analytics stack prefers parquet for heavy traces but CSV is easier for quick review.
[04:09] Carlos: propose two outputs: compressed parquet for the full per-request dump and a summarized CSV for executive deck (one row per percentile + aggregated metrics).
[04:19] Samir: what columns do you want in the summary CSV?
[04:22] Leah: suggested columns: timestamp_window, model_variant, total_requests, avg_latency_ms, p50_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, avg_tokens_in, avg_tokens_out, cache_hit_rate, accuracy_percent, sample_failure_count, notes.
[04:40] Jordan: add 'sequence_length_bucket' maybe top/median/95th.
[04:44] Carlos: we'll add that as separate breakdown. Also add 'cost_estimate_usd' per 1M tokens for the run for budgeting.
[04:52] Maya: yes we'll surface an estimated cost line item in the executive summary.
[04:56] Samir: any concerns around data retention and logs? We need them for two weeks for debugging and then they must be purged.
[05:03] Priya: security requirement: logs stored encrypted at rest and keys in our KMS. If you need access to our KMS for test runs we need to discuss enterprise private deployment.
[05:13] Maya: call that out as a gating question — for this POC we can stage logs in Redwood's secure storage with customer-managed KMS if you provide the key or we can run in your private deployment. We'll list both options in the rubric.
[05:28] Jordan: timeline check: we want signoff by end of Feb to align with a March pilot. Is that realistic?
[05:34] Carlos: yes if we get traces by 2/18 we can schedule the benchmark window for the last week of Feb. Run takes about 3 business days plus 48 hours for result validation.
[05:43] Leah: deliverable cadence: Redwood shares gating rubric (this doc) and report template by 2/14; customer shares traces and allowlist info by 2/18; benchmark window 2/24-2/28; results and exec summary delivered by 3/03.
[05:58] Samir: who signs the final acceptance? Product or ML?
[06:02] Jordan: Product owns sign-off (Samir) with technical concurrence from ML (Jordan) and infra (Priya).
[06:11] Maya: good, we'll include a signature block in the executive report for Product, ML, and Infra.
[06:18] Carlos: little nit: we should define exactly how we compute 'accuracy_percent' for ambiguous open-answer prompts — will you provide exact answer tokens or labels?
[06:27] Samir: for free-form we will provide 3 human raters and an agreement threshold — we'll produce a binary pass for each example and then accuracy is percent passing.
[06:35] Leah: perfect, we'll include human-eval sampling methodology in the appendix of the report — sampling rate, seed set, rater instructions.
[06:44] Jordan: one more ask — include a short runbook for us to reproduce the benchmark internally; we may want to run the same test later.
[06:51] Maya: agreed, runbook will be appended.
[06:54] Priya: minor network note, we might do an isolated run inside our VPC to measure true latency; that's preferred for P99.
[07:02] Carlos: ok if we do that we'll need an agent inside your VPC or direct peering. That affects scheduling and permissions.
[07:10] Samir: okay let's assume two modes: Redwood-hosted sim (faster to run) and VPC-peered run (best effort for final P99). We'll mark the peered run as hard requirement for green.
[07:22] Maya: that becomes part of the matrix: final green requires VPC-peered validated P99.
[07:27] Jordan: understood.
[07:30] (brief mute/unmute noise)
[07:33] Maya: recap of concrete deliverables: gating rubric + report template by 2/14; Redwood to provide parquet + CSV schema; customer to deliver traces and allowlist by 2/18; benchmark window 2/24-2/28; results 3/03. Any objections?
[07:51] Jordan: none here, sounds good.
[07:53] Samir: fine.
[07:55] Priya: ok.
[07:57] Maya: awesome, I'll send the doc and template after the call and include proposed mitigation steps for yellow outcomes.
[08:03] Carlos: quick note — mention of competitors, Jordan: you mentioned Anthropic and Vertex during procurement?
[08:09] Jordan: yeah we're also vetting managed Vertex endpoints for their integrations, and Anthropic for safety posture, but right now focus is on latency/cost tradeoff.
[08:17] Leah: noted.
[08:19] Maya: last thing — do we want an executive 1-pager format? We can auto-generate a 1-slide summary.
[08:24] Samir: yes please.
[08:26] Maya: great. Thanks everyone, I'll follow up with the artifacts. End call.

Meeting end.
